cios, totoq; caelestium amore atq; desiderio ardere si-
mulant: cùm non aliud quærant, quàm ut suis
commodis & priuatæ existimationi consulãt. Ta-
les olim cum tota factione sua Corita fuerunt,
qui totius Ecclesiæ caussam agere volebant videri, ut &
hanc ex Mosis atque Aaronis manu eriperent,
& Deo suum honorem atque cultum vindicarent.
Num.16. Tales Prophetarum temporibus mul-
ti erant, quos canes mutos dicit Isaias cap. 56.
qui item (ut Micheas cap. 2. ait) de vino & sicera
concionabantur, & populum inanibus promissis
lactabant. Similes horum erant Pharisæi, Scribæ
& Sacerdotes, qui cùm Mosis cathedram occupas-
sent, populum inani traditionum fuco decipiebant,
&sub longarum precationum prætextu domos vi-
duarum & orphanorum devorabant. Huius
generis impostores nouissimis temporibus passim ex-
orituros esse, Christus & Apostoli prædixerunt: &
verè quidem hoc prædictum fuisse, res ipsa loquitur,
si quid inter Christianos ab annis quingentis fa-
ctum fit, ex historiis animo repetas, & quid quotidie
fiat paulo attentius obserues.

page.notes: The word "admonere" in the second paragraph is partly overprinted by a faint mark, so its letters are uncertain. The "Num.16." reference is set at the start of a text line, not in a margin. "Isaias" has an unclear first letter (I or J). Some "u" and "v" spellings were normalised as instructed. Many long s were written as plain s. Show-through from the reverse is present but was not transcribed.
